submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 remains far above the 2 mg/L hard limit (min observed ~9.0 mg/L; t=52 value ~11.7 mg/L), product assays show normal accumulation (3.23 g/L at t=239), and all three source batches — which the receiving trajectory closely tracks — maintain DO well above the limit through 479 h while producing 6.4–7.0 g/L. No intervention is warranted: any feed reduction would sacrifice product mass and any aeration increase is unnecessary; stop would zero production despite a stable, oxygen-rich process.
submission.uncertainty: Source and receiving processes differ; hidden receiving parameters could raise oxygen demand beyond source history. However the receiving DO track so far closely matches the source batches (which never approach 2 mg/L), giving a wide margin (>7 mg/L at the worst observed points). Residual risk is low but not zero; sensor noise and assay delays mean a rare excursion could go undetected between samples. One extra product assay was considered but not needed, as the latest assay already confirms healthy production.

Physical forward model, KEEP: post-decision min DO 8.73 mg/L, product mass 576.3 kg, post_decision_feasible=true
Physical forward model, combined: post-decision min DO 10.00 mg/L (sensitivity range 8.93-10.85), product mass 595.5 kg, feasible

submission.rationale: All bounded plans are predicted feasible with DO far above the 2 mg/L hard limit (receiving DO sensor ~9.2 mg/L at 52 h, no near-limit trend; forward model min DO 8.7-10.0 post-decision). No stop is warranted. Among feasible plans, combined (feed x0.8, air x1.15) retains the most product mass: 595.5 kg vs 576.3 kg for KEEP/increase_air (a ~19 kg gain), while simultaneously giving the highest oxygen margin (min DO 10.0 mg/L nominal, worst sensitivity member 8.93 mg/L). reduce_feed yields the same mass but a lower DO margin, so combined dominates on both priorities: constraint robustness and product mass. This is a model-based recommendation, not an approval, and the forward model is a source-calibrated nominal prediction, not truth.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated; the receiving process may differ from source. However, the constraint margin is large (~9 mg/L observed, ~8.9 mg/L worst-case sensitivity member vs 2 mg/L limit), so even substantial model mismatch is unlikely to threaten feasibility. The product-mass advantage of combined (~19 kg, consistent across all 5 sensitivity members) is also robust in sign. Residual risks: unmodeled receiving-specific dynamics, assay delays, and the possibility that feed reduction slows production beyond model prediction; these are bounded by the wide DO headroom.
